{{Infobox football tournament season | image = |country=[[Peru]] |dates={{nowrap|21 June – 7 November 2019}} | winners = [[Atlético Grau]] (1st title) |second=[[Sport Huancayo]] |continental_cup_title = [[2020 Copa Sudamericana|Copa Sudamericana]] |continental_cup_qualifiers =Atlético Grau |num_teams=30 |matches=59 |goals=161 | biggest home win = | biggest away win = | highest scoring = |scoring_leader =[[Carlos Neumann]] (6 goals) | prev_season = | next_season = [[2021 Copa Bicentenario|2021]] }} The '''2019 Copa Bicenterio''' was the 1st edition of the [[Copa Bicentenario]], the new national cup competition of [[Peru]]. It was played between June and July while the [[Peru national football team]] prepared for and competed in the [[2019 Copa América]]. The tournament was played as a knockout competition, with the participation of the 18 teams of the [[Peruvian Primera División|Liga 1]], and 12 teams of the [[Segunda División Peruana|Liga 2]]. The champions qualified for the [[2020 Copa Sudamericana]] and [[2020 Supercopa Peruana|Supercopa Peruana]]. [[Atlético Grau]] were winners of the competition, beating [[Sport Huancayo]] 4-3 on penalties, winning their first Copa Bicentenario and professional title. == Format == This year's edition used a group stage and knockout stage format. The first stage was played with all 30 teams, each being split into 8 groups of either 3 or 4. Each team plays each other once and the top two advance to the knockout stage. Starting from this point, the cup was played as a single-elimination tournament, with all subsequent rounds being played as one-legged series. == Schedule == The schedule of the competition was as follows: {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: center" !Round !First leg |- |Group stage |21 June – 8 July 2019 |- |Knockout stage |10 August – 7 November 2019 |- |Round of 16 |10 August – 12 August 2019 |- |Quarter-finals |3 September – 5 September 2019 |- |Semi-finals |25 – 17 October 2019 |- |Final |7 November 2019 |} ==Teams== 30 teams took part in the tournament, 18 of the [[2019 Liga 1 (Peru)|2019 Liga 1]] and 12 of the [[2019 Liga 2 (Peru)|Liga 2]]. ===Stadia and locations=== {{location map+ |Peru |float=right |width=550 |caption=Locations of the 2019 Liga 1 and Liga 2 teams |places= {{location map~ |Peru |lat=-13.525 |long=-71.972222 |label=
